transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's nice to meet you too. Um, honestly, what made me finally come in is that I keep getting up during these long sales strategy meetings at work. I know I’m supposed to just stay seated, but I end up getting out of my chair anyway... even if it’s just to go refill my water or pace by the printer for a bit.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized or “up” compared with your normal self?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I have good days where I'm in a good mood, but I wouldn't say I've ever felt unusually energized or... up compared to my normal self. It's really just my regular baseline.
When you get up during those meetings, is it because you feel worried or on edge?

No, not at all. I don't feel worried or anxious when I do it. It’s more just... I get really restless. I just feel this physical need to stretch my legs or move around a bit, but it really has nothing to do with feeling on edge or stressed about the meeting.

latest_inference.note: Restlessness is not driven by worry/on-edge feelings, which argues against F41.1. Denies unusually elevated/energized states, reducing concern for a bipolar-spectrum explanation. Current presentation most strongly fits F90.0.
